newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president to sign 1997 national budget.
newsitem.headline: Polish president to sign 1997 national budget.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski will sign into law the 1997 national budget draft, approved by lower house of parliament last week, his senior aide said on Monday.
"If no major changes are introduced (by the Senate),... I do not see any threats to the budget from the president," Marek Siwiec, a minister in the presidential chancery, told a weekly news briefing.
Kwasniewski was widely expected to sign the bill, prepared by the government, dominated by his political allies, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance.
The lower house passed the budget draft on Friday. The Senate, which has a month to analyse it, is not expected to propose any major amendments.

The budget, with deficit set at 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, envisages cutting year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December 1997, from 18.5 percent last year, while keeping the economic growth at 5.5 percent.
